subject: Install non-compiled version of R-INLA on a HPC cluster

messages.author: 10edd14eaa782c14
messages.subject: Install non-compiled version of R-INLA on a HPC cluster
parts:
Hello R-INLA users,

I am interested in installing R-INLA on an HPC cluster. When I spoke with an admin, they said that the non-compiled version would need to be installed so that it is compatible with the current OS and shared libraries.

They can work with the github source (https://github.com/hrue/r-inla) but couldn't find the installation instructions. I am wondering if installation instructions can be provided.

Thank you.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Install non-compiled version of R-INLA on a HPC cluster
parts:
the normal thing to do (which we also do), is to install the R-INLA
package as normal with R-4.1, then download and install new binaries for
the inla program and the fmesher program,

> inla.binary.install()
* Looking for Version_22.01.25 and os='<choose interactively>'
Available alternatives:
Alternative 1 is ./CentOS Linux-6
(Core)/Version_22.01.25/64bit.tgz
Alternative 2 is ./CentOS Linux-7
(Core)/Version_22.01.25/64bit.tgz
Alternative 3 is ./CentOS Stream-
8/Version_22.01.25/64bit.tgz
Alternative 4 is ./Fedora Linux-35 (Workstation
Edition)/Version_22.01.25/64bit.tgz
Alternative 5 is ./Manjaro Linux-/Version_22.01.25/64bit.tgz
Alternative 6 is ./Ubuntu-18.04.6 LTS (Bionic
Beaver)/Version_22.01.25/64bit.tgz
Alternative 7 is ./Ubuntu-20.04.3 LTS (Focal
Fossa)/Version_22.01.25/64bit.tgz
Chose alternative [1:7]
1:



'CentOS Linux-7' is normally a good choice. Can you check with the HPC
team is one of these binary builds would be ok? Otherwise, you can
compile these binaries yourself and just use with the package itself.

Best
H
